Capacity without visible construction is not the same measure as the share of AI projects, and expected future delays are not proof that nearly every project was already late. The universal loss assertion also lacks a defined population and accounting basis.
limitations: The financial component cannot receive a supported or contradicted score with an unknown accounting basis.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI bubble has every big warning sign: every company loses money, seemingly every AI data center is behind schedule, and the vast majority of them aren't even under construction.

statement.excerpt: The AI bubble has every big, flashing warning sign you could ask for. Every company loses money. Seemingly every AI data center is behind schedule, and the vast majority of them aren’t even under construction.

from_speaker: Seemingly every AI data center is behind schedule
the vast majority of them aren’t even under construction
our_interpretation: The warning-sign language is rhetorical; the loss, delay, and construction assertions are the checkable components.
The surrounding discussion principally concerns AI labs and startups buying compute. Whether 'every company' also includes chip suppliers and diversified technology companies is unresolved.
The ordinary reading of 'loses money' is an overall loss, not simply expenditure or negative cash flow.
For the financial component, 2025 is the latest completed annual reporting period before the post; the claim does not supply a common quarterly reporting period.

Construction and schedule status refer to the state immediately before the April 8 post, informed by the latest available pre-post observations. The target interval bounds these different component periods; they are not interchangeable.
'Vast majority' means substantially more than half of announced AI data-center projects by count. I do not substitute capacity in gigawatts or invent a percentage threshold.
'Seemingly' qualifies the delay assertion; it is not a conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A defined population shows overall losses for every included company, nearly universal delays against original schedules, and a substantially greater-than-half share of announced AI data-center projects without construction underway.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable financial records identify a profitable company within the intended population, or representative project records show that delays are not nearly universal or that most projects are already under construction.

evidence.explanation: The tracker reports substantial unbuilt capacity and anticipates delays affecting part of the 2026 pipeline. Its figures concern capacity in a selected large-data-center population, so they do not directly measure the asserted share of AI projects or establish that nearly all were already late.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defined company population with comparable financial results, plus a pre-post project register showing original schedules and construction status by project count.
